name: paint
summary: Paint things as a spray can does (no paint used), one colour for reference_ids or a colour each with items; with neither, list the colours.

help.text: Uses the game's own paint: synced to clients and saved. A colour is a name (any case, as the colour list gives it), an index, or 'default' for the thing's own prefab colour. Each result gives previous_color, so a later items call can put the old colours back.
help.keys: colors [{index, name, paint_only}], count, results, success_count, error_count.

colours.summary: The colour list and paint_only colours.
colours.text: With no targets it answers colors [{index, name, paint_only}] and count. paint_only colours (the metallic cans) cannot be set through logic but can be sprayed.

reply.summary: Each result and how a colour reads.
reply.text: results, one per thing: {index, ok, reference_id, previous_color, color}, or {index, ok: false, reference_id, previous_color, error}; plus count, success_count and error_count. A colour is {index, name, is_default}: is_default is the prefab's own colour; index and name are null when the thing has no colour; a thing whose colour is a state gives the state colour it shows, as the Color logic type reads it.

refusals.summary: Why one thing is not painted.
refusals.text: Per thing: thing_not_found; not_paintable (no paintable material, or a batched structure the game cannot repaint); has_color_state (its colour is a state set through the Color logic type, such as an LED display; lights paint); invalid_color (unknown name or index, or 'default' on a thing with no prefab colour); paint_failed (the colour did not change); invalid_argument (an id that is not a decimal string, a colour that is not a string).

reference_ids.description: Things to paint the one color, up to 256.

color.description: With reference_ids: a colour name ('Blue'), an index ('3'), or 'default'.
A colour name, an index, or 'default'.

items.description: Up to 256 {reference_id, color} pairs, a colour each; puts back previous_color values.
